stories.article_text_excerpt: Image source, EPA Image caption, David McBride pleaded guilty to leaking military secrets to the media in 2023 By Lana Lam Sydney Published 4 hours ago A whistleblower jailed for leaking military secrets about Australia's involvement in Afghanistan has been released on parole after serving 27 months. In 2024, David McBride was sentenced to five years and eight months after pleading guilty to stealing top secret defence documents and giving it to the media. His actions later led to a landmark inquiry that found evidence that Australian forces had unlawfully killed 39 Afghans during the war. On Thursday, a spokesperson for the Attorney-General Michelle Rowland said McBride's "parole was considered and granted". The ex-military lawyer, who is being treated for lung cancer, will serve the rest of his sentence in the community under supervision. Shortly after the decision, advocacy group The Information Rights Project released a statement on McBride's behalf, according to national broadcaster ABC. Israel and Ukraine are among the countries the rule could affect, with both having enjoyed recent success in the competition. What did the Eurovision organizers say? The symbolic step is part of new Prime Minister Peter Magyar's sweeping efforts to dismantle the legacy of former premier Viktor Orban after winning April's general elections . Baka was a staunch critic of Orban who was removed from his Supreme Court role during the former PM's tenure. Now, he will replace Tamas Sulyok, a president appointed by Orban , whose term in office was shortened via constitutional amendment in order to remove him from the largely ceremonial role. After around 12 hours of debate, lawmakers voted 468 to 88 in favor of the 12-article bill, with six abstentions. It was backed by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's AK Party , its nationalist MHP allies and the pro- Kurdish DEM party. What does Turkey's new PKK law provide? The law sets out procedures for the PKK's disarmament and dissolution and the reintegration of some members into civilian life. The government has stressed that it is not a general amnesty. "We're not at war, but we are the daily target of hybrid warfare," Dobrindt told the newspaper Bild am Sonntag following the discovery of a drone carrying explosives at Leipzig/Halle Airport. "Espionage, sabotage, cyberattacks, or covert operations by foreign powers aimed at destabilizing Germany or inflicting direct harm are a constant reality," Dobrindt said. He also noted that the country is stepping up research into drones to address new security threats . A new drone security research center will be established later in August at a German Aerospace Center (DLR) test airport in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt , Dobrindt said.
